problems.quote: “All A are B” + “Some B are C” → “Some A are C” (definite)
problems.problem: The middle term B is undistributed in both premises (predicate of universal affirmative and subject of particular affirmative), so no valid conclusion follows; “Some A are C” is not definite.
problems.correction: “All A are B” + “Some B are C” yields no definite conclusion (undistributed middle).
problems.verifierReason: Original conclusion invalid; correction correctly states no definite conclusion.

problems.quote: A complementary pair in syllogism consists of two conclusions that cannot both be false at the same time. The classic forms are the contradictory pair and the contrary pair
problems.problem: Contrary pair (A vs E) can both be false; only contradictory pairs (A vs O, E vs I) cannot both be false. The either-or option requires contradictories, not contraries.
problems.correction: A complementary pair for either-or consists of contradictory conclusions (A vs O, E vs I) that cannot both be false and cannot both be true.
problems.verifierReason: Original definition incorrect; correction accurately describes contradictory pair as complementary.

problems.quote: the middle term C is distributed in the universal
problems.problem: In “All A are C”, the predicate C is undistributed; only the subject A is distributed. Therefore the middle term is not distributed, and no conclusion follows.
problems.correction: the middle term C is undistributed in “All A are C”, so no conclusion follows.
problems.verifierReason: Original claim of distribution false; correction correctly notes C is undistributed.

problems.quote: the middle term C is not distributed in “All C are D”
problems.problem: In “All C are D”, the subject C is distributed. The failure to derive “No A are D” is due to invalid syllogistic form, not distribution of C.
problems.correction: C is distributed in “All C are D”; “No A are D” cannot be derived because the premises do not support it.
problems.verifierReason: Original claim of non‑distribution false; correction correctly states C is distributed and no conclusion follows.

problems.quote: The valid conclusion is “Some A are not C” (O)
problems.problem: The syllogism “No A are B” (E) + “Some B are not C” (O) is invalid (mood EO in Figure 1); no conclusion follows.
problems.correction: No valid conclusion follows; the mood EO-1 is invalid.
problems.verifierReason: Original conclusion invalid; correction correctly says no valid conclusion can be drawn.
